claims.text: A Pt/Cu single-atom alloy consists of Pt atoms diluted and individually isolated within Cu nanoparticles or a Cu matrix.
Isolating Pt in Cu reduces the binding energy of reactive intermediates such as CO or coke precursors.
A Pt/Cu SAA has greater catalytic activity and durability than a catalyst containing aggregated Pt sites.
A low-Pt, moderate-Cu Pt/Cu/γ-Al2O3 catalyst will contain partially clustered Pt.
Increasing Cu dilution at fixed Pt loading can produce a Pt/Cu SAA.
Decreasing Pt loading at fixed Cu content can preserve or promote the Pt/Cu SAA structure.
Approximately 500°C is a typical temperature for evaluating Pt/Cu catalysts in dehydrogenation reactions.
Atomic isolation of Pt within Cu produces a modified electronic environment at the Pt atoms.
Ligand and ensemble effects from surrounding Cu atoms weaken adsorption at isolated Pt atoms.
Propylene interacts more weakly with Pt/Cu SAA sites than with Pt nanoparticles.
Weaker adsorbate interaction minimizes carbon deposition on active Pt sites and helps preserve catalytic activity.
Moderating adsorption strength according to the Sabatier principle improves catalytic performance by avoiding over-strong adsorption and poisoning.
Under identical propane-dehydrogenation conditions, a highly Cu-diluted Pt/Cu SAA will have higher activity than a lower-Cu catalyst with aggregated Pt.
The Pt/Cu SAA will accumulate less coke than the aggregated-Pt baseline.
The Pt/Cu SAA will retain activity longer than the aggregated-Pt baseline.
At the same overall Pt loading, lowering Cu dilution permits Pt aggregation on γ-Al2O3.
The proposed mechanism should apply when catalytic behavior is dominated by intermediate adsorption energies and Cu does not introduce competing pathways.

contradictions.description: The phrase 'decrease the Pt loading while keeping Pt constant' is internally contradictory because Pt loading cannot simultaneously decrease and remain constant.
The intervention offers decreasing Pt loading as an alternative, whereas the baseline and falsification experiment require identical overall Pt loadings; these define different comparisons.
